role: The base material: every block's Material answers canBurn, isSolid, isOpaque, isReplaceable, mobility, whether the block is passable for pistons and doors, and the adventure-mode dig exemption.

members.name: canBurn
members.note: the canBurn column, generated from the live objects by make -C oracle blocks-h

members.name: isAdventureModeExempt
members.note: only EntityPlayer.isCurrentToolAdventureModeExempt reads it, in adventure mode; the game is survival

members.name: materialMapColor
members.note: map colors are not needed (see the MapColor record)

members.name: field_76235_h
members.note: the pushReaction copy, set by setPushReaction and read only by pistons

members.name: pushReaction
members.note: pistons do not exist in the native engine; the field is read nowhere that runs

members.name: blocksLight
members.note: the opacity column decides light blocking per block; the material-level isOpaque chain feeds it

members.name: setReplaceable
members.note: the constructor chain that set the column is in the oracle the table is generated from

members.name: setBlocksLight
members.note: folded into the opaque column by the generator

members.name: setNoToolMobility
members.note: mobility values live in the MATERIALS rows; the exact per-material mobility factor was not re-read column by column

members.name: getMobilityFlag
members.note: the Java-side EnumMobility wrapper; the native reads the mobility number directly

members.name: isToolNotRequired
members.note: the material == this test lives in harvest.c's tool-required check

members.name: setAdventureModeExempt
members.note: never called by any 1.7.10 material constructor, so the field stays false and has no column

members.name: getMaterialMobility
members.note: only Block.getMobilityFlag reads it; only BlockPistonBase calls getMobilityFlag, when a piston extends or retracts; with world.conf redstone = off no piston ever moves

notes: The MATERIALS table (blocks.h:16) is generated by netherite.oracle.BlockTable from the live 1.7.10 objects via make -C oracle biomes-h, so every column is the oracle's own value rather than a hand transcription. test_worldgen.c and test_move.c exercise the material fields through terrain and movement.
